subject: History
description: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1772-1833) — Brahmo Samaj founder, Sati abolition, social reform, Father of Modern India.

questions.stem: Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often called the FATHER OF:
questions.explanation: RAJA RAM MOHAN ROY (22 May 1772 - 27 September 1833) — called 'FATHER OF MODERN INDIA' / 'FATHER OF INDIAN RENAISSANCE' / 'FATHER OF BENGAL RENAISSANCE'. KEY ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) Founded BRAHMO SAMAJ (1828) — reformist Hindu monotheistic movement; rejected idol worship, polytheism, caste discrimination, child marriage, sati. (2) CRUSADED AGAINST SATI (widow self-immolation) → Lord William Bentinck's SATI ABOLITION ACT 1829 (XVII of 1829) — landmark social reform. (3) Promoted ENGLISH EDUCATION + Western science alongside Sanskrit + Persian education. (4) Started newspapers + journals: SAMBAD KAUMUDI (Bengali, 1821), MIRAT-UL-AKHBAR (Persian). (5) Translated Upanishads + Vedanta into English. (6) Advocated WIDOW REMARRIAGE, abolition of POLYGAMY, INHERITANCE rights for women. KEY TITLES: (a) 'Father of Modern India' — given by various scholars including S.D. Collet, biographer. (b) Title 'RAJA' was conferred on him by MUGHAL Emperor AKBAR II (1830) — for representing the emperor's case to the British. DEATH: died in BRISTOL, ENGLAND (27 Sept 1833) on a diplomatic mission for the Mughal court; buried in Arno's Vale Cemetery there. His tomb was later erected with funds raised by Brahmo Samaj. UPSC ANGLE: 19TH century social reform — GS-1 modern history; GS-4 ethics (women's rights, social reform). PYQ FREQUENCY: Ram Mohan Roy in UPSC, MPSC, SSC modern history — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: BRAHMO SAMAJ was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in:
questions.explanation: BRAHMO SAMAJ (originally BRAHMO SABHA) — founded by Ram Mohan Roy on 20 AUGUST 1828 in CALCUTTA. PHILOSOPHY: monotheistic; worship of formless ONE GOD (Brahman); rejected: (a) Idolatry. (b) Caste discrimination. (c) Religious orthodoxy + meaningless rituals. (d) Sati. (e) Child marriage. (f) Polygamy. ACCEPTED: (a) Universal religion. (b) Reason + science. (c) Education for all. (d) Women's emancipation. KEY LEADERS POST-Ram Mohan: (1) DEBENDRANATH TAGORE (Rabindranath's father) — joined 1843; led organization 1843-1858. (2) KESHAB CHANDRA SEN — radical leader; created BRAHMO SAMAJ OF INDIA (1866 split from Adi Brahmo Samaj). (3) Pratap Chandra Mozoomdar, Rabindranath Tagore (philosophical inheritor). RELATED REFORM ORGANIZATIONS: (1) PRARTHANA SAMAJ (1867) — Maharashtra branch; founder R.G. BHANDARKAR + others; M.G. RANADE active member. (2) ARYA SAMAJ (1875) — by SWAMI DAYANANDA SARASWATI; emphasized Vedas; 'Back to Vedas' movement. (3) RAMAKRISHNA MISSION (1897) — by SWAMI VIVEKANANDA. (4) THEOSOPHICAL SOCIETY (1875) — Madame Blavatsky, Col. Olcott; later Annie Besant. (5) ALIGARH MOVEMENT (1875) — Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. UPSC angle: SOCIO-RELIGIOUS REFORMS in 19th-century India — GS-1; comparative analysis of reform movements. PYQ FREQUENCY: Brahmo Samaj founding year + leaders in UPSC, MPSC, SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: SATI ABOLITION ACT (1829) was passed by which Governor-General with Ram Mohan Roy's support?
questions.explanation: LORD WILLIAM BENTINCK (1828-35, 1st Governor-General of British India under 1833 Charter Act) — passed SATI ABOLITION REGULATION on 4 DECEMBER 1829 (Regulation XVII of 1829, Bengal Presidency; later extended to Madras + Bombay). KEY: criminalized SATI (or sahamarana — voluntary or forced widow self-immolation on husband's funeral pyre); offenders punishable as murderers. PRECONDITIONS: Ram Mohan Roy's persistent advocacy + petitions + writings + public pressure since ~1818. STATISTICS: ~700-800 sati cases recorded annually in Bengal in early 1800s. POST-ACT: orthodox Hindu groups initially OPPOSED via 'Dharma Sabha' (Calcutta, 1830); appealed to Privy Council in London — Privy Council in 1832 UPHELD the ban. Ram Mohan Roy went to England partly to argue this case. OTHER REFORMS by BENTINCK: (1) Abolition of THUGGEE (organized robber-murderer cult) — under Col. WILLIAM SLEEMAN (1830s). (2) Abolition of FEMALE INFANTICIDE in some communities. (3) ENGLISH as language of higher education + courts (Macaulay's MINUTE 1835 — under Bentinck). (4) Abolition of slavery (later, 1843 by Ellenborough's Act). LATER SATI REGULATIONS: SATI PREVENTION ACT 1987 (after Roop Kanwar incident in Rajasthan, 4 Sept 1987 — last documented sati case); declared sati + glorification of sati as criminal offences. UPSC angle: 19th-century social reform; women's rights timeline. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sati abolition in UPSC, MPSC, SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Ram Mohan Roy promoted English education in opposition to which group's traditional Sanskrit education?
questions.explanation: ORIENTALIST vs ANGLICIST debate (1820s-1830s) was a major colonial education-policy debate: (1) ORIENTALISTS (e.g., H.H. Wilson, Sir William Jones, Henry Princep) — advocated continued use of CLASSICAL SANSKRIT/ARABIC/PERSIAN education for Indians. (2) ANGLICISTS (e.g., Lord Macaulay, William Bentinck, Charles Trevelyan) — argued for ENGLISH-medium education + Western sciences/literature. RAM MOHAN ROY was on the ANGLICIST side: he wrote a letter to Lord Amherst (1823) arguing AGAINST establishing a Sanskrit College for traditional learning, INSTEAD favoring SCIENCE + MATH + WESTERN learning. RATIONALE: (a) Scientific knowledge is in EUROPEAN languages now; modern education needed. (b) Limited resources should fund modern, not antiquated, learning. (c) English would open careers in govt + commerce. KEY MILESTONES: (1) HINDU COLLEGE Calcutta (1817) — co-founded by Ram Mohan Roy + David Hare; English-medium; later became Presidency College + Presidency University. (2) MACAULAY's MINUTE (1835) — settled the debate; English became OFFICIAL medium. (3) WOOD'S DESPATCH (1854) — 'Magna Carta of Indian Education'; established UNIVERSITIES of Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857). (4) RAJA RADHAKANTA DEB (~1838) opposed Roy's reform views — orthodox; founded Dharma Sabha. UPSC angle: education policy in colonial India + role in nationalism. PYQ FREQUENCY: orientalist-anglicist debate in UPSC, MPSC, SSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which BENGALI WEEKLY newspaper was started by Ram Mohan Roy in 1821?
questions.explanation: SAMBAD KAUMUDI ('Moon of Intelligence' / 'Moon of News') — Bengali weekly newspaper started by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 4 DECEMBER 1821 in CALCUTTA. PURPOSE: to disseminate REFORMIST ideas, social-reform debates, modern thought to Bengali public. CONTENT: anti-sati editorials, anti-caste, women's rights, education, science, news. ALSO BY ROY: (1) MIRAT-UL-AKHBAR — Persian-language journal (1822-1823); discontinued after British press regulations (1823) restricted vernacular press. KEY EARLY INDIAN NEWSPAPERS / JOURNALS (memorize): (1) BENGAL GAZETTE (1780) — first Indian newspaper, by JAMES AUGUSTUS HICKY; called 'Hicky's Gazette'. (2) BANGAL DARPAN (1818) — by Ram Mohan + others; Bengali. (3) SAMBAD KAUMUDI (1821) — Bengali. (4) MIRAT-UL-AKHBAR (1822) — Persian. (5) SAMACHAR DARPAN (1818) — by Serampore Baptist Mission; Bengali. (6) BANGADOOT (1829) — by Roy. (7) SOMPRAKASH (1858) — by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. (8) KESARI + MARATHA (1881) — by BAL GANGADHAR TILAK. (9) HINDU (1878, ENGLISH) — Madras; founded by G. Subramania Iyer + others. (10) AMRITA BAZAR PATRIKA (1868) — Bengal. (11) THE TRIBUNE (1881) — Punjab. PRESS REGULATIONS history: ADAMS REGULATIONS (1823) — restricted vernacular press; METCALFE'S 1835 LIBERATION; LYTTON'S VERNACULAR PRESS ACT 1878 (anti-Indian); REPEALED 1881 by Lord Ripon. UPSC angle: print media + colonial governance. PYQ FREQUENCY: Indian newspaper history in UPSC, MPSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Ram Mohan Roy died in 1833 in which country?
questions.explanation: RAM MOHAN ROY DIED on 27 SEPTEMBER 1833 in BRISTOL, England, age 61, of MENINGITIS. He was on an OFFICIAL DIPLOMATIC mission representing AKBAR II (Mughal Emperor) to discuss the EMPEROR'S PENSION + STIPEND with the BRITISH KING WILLIAM IV + East India Company directors. The mission also addressed RIGHTS related to the Mughal household. ARRIVAL IN ENGLAND: April 1831 in LIVERPOOL; received by British political/intellectual circles with great respect. He met King William IV; was the first INDIAN of high rank to visit England in this manner. WHILE IN ENGLAND: (1) Argued against repeal of Sati Abolition Act (Privy Council had upheld it 1832 — Roy's testimony key). (2) Lobbied for the Mughal pension. (3) Met JEREMY BENTHAM, Robert Owen, other British thinkers. (4) Toured England, France. BURIAL: ARNO'S VALE CEMETERY, BRISTOL. Tomb constructed 1843 by Dwarkanath Tagore (Brahmo Samaj patron, Rabindranath's grandfather) using funds raised by Brahmo Samaj. The Tomb is a popular pilgrimage site for Indian visitors to UK. STATUE in Bristol: 1997 BHASKAR ROY built statue near Bristol Council House. POST-INDIA: BRAHMO SAMAJ continued under Debendranath Tagore + Keshab Chandra Sen; eventually contributed to broader Indian Renaissance + nationalism. UPSC angle: ROY's role symbolizes early Indian engagement with WESTERN modernity + diplomacy. PYQ FREQUENCY: Roy's death location in UPSC, MPSC 1× per 2 cycles.

questions.stem: Ram Mohan Roy translated which Sanskrit text into ENGLISH (a key cultural-bridging contribution)?
questions.explanation: Ram Mohan Roy translated several UPANISHADS + VEDANTA texts into ENGLISH. KEY WORKS: (1) Translation of KENA, ISHA, KATHA, MUNDAKA UPANISHADS into English (1816-1819). (2) Books expounding UPANISHADIC philosophy + monotheism. (3) 'A Defence of Hindu Theism' — criticized idolatry. (4) 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' (1804, in Persian + Arabic) — 'Gift to Monotheists' — early work questioning religious orthodoxy. (5) 'Precepts of Jesus' (1820) — extracted moral teachings of Jesus, set aside miracles + theological claims. PURPOSE: to show that HINDUISM at its philosophical core is MONOTHEISTIC; idolatry is later corruption. INFLUENCE in UK: his English-language scholarship gave WESTERN audiences direct access to Hindu philosophy; influenced TRANSCENDENTALISTS (Emerson, Thoreau in USA) and THEOSOPHISTS (Madame Blavatsky). PARALLEL to DARA SHIKOH (Mughal prince, 1657) who translated Upanishads into PERSIAN — Ram Mohan continued this cross-cultural tradition into English. PROFOUND SCHOLARLY contribution: he was conversant in SANSKRIT, ARABIC, PERSIAN, BENGALI, ENGLISH, HEBREW, GREEK — Renaissance-style polyglot. WORKS IN BENGALI: 'Vedant Grantha' (1815), 'Vedantasara' — popularizing Hindu philosophy. POETRY in Persian. UPSC ANGLE: BENGAL RENAISSANCE figures + their LITERARY contributions; Indian thought + Western interaction. PYQ FREQUENCY: Roy's literary works in UPSC, MPSC History optional, SSC GA 1× per cycle.
